cards.front: MCQ (Q1.1): Simplify 2x − x(x + y). Options: A x²+xy  B 2x−x²−xy  C x²−xy  D 2x−x²+xy.
cards.back:
Answer: B.
Distribute the −x: 2x − x(x + y) = 2x − x·x − x·y = 2x − x² − xy.
Watch the sign: the minus in front of x multiplies BOTH terms in the bracket, making both negative.
cards.source: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016
cards.sourceFile: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016.yml

cards.front: MCQ (Q1.2): The number 1 is NOT a(n)... A rational number  B whole number  C irrational number  D integer.
cards.back:
Answer: C (irrational number).
1 IS rational (1/1), IS a whole number, and IS an integer. An irrational number is one with a non-recurring, non-terminating decimal — 1 is not irrational, so the odd one out is C.
cards.source: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016
cards.sourceFile: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016.yml

cards.front: MCQ (Q1.3): All fractions can be written as a(n)... A percentage  B decimal  C ratio  D option A; B and C.
cards.back:
Answer: D (option A; B and C).
A fraction can be expressed as a percentage, a decimal AND a ratio — these are three different ways of expressing the same fraction, so all apply.

cards.front: MCQ (Q1.4): Simplify √(16x⁴/y¹⁶). Options: A 4x²/y⁴  B 8x²/y⁸  C 8x²/y⁴  D 4x²/y⁸.
cards.back:
Answer: D (4x²/y⁸).
Take the square root of each part: √16 = 4; √(x⁴) = x² (halve the exponent); √(y¹⁶) = y⁸ (halve the exponent).
So √(16x⁴/y¹⁶) = 4x²/y⁸. To root a power, halve its exponent.
cards.source: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016

cards.front: MCQ (Q1.5): Find the missing number in the sequence 2 ; 5 ; 10 ; ... ; 26. Options: A 15  B 25  C 17  D 20.
cards.back:
Answer: C (17).
The pattern of first differences is +3, +5, +7, +9: 2 →(+3) 5 →(+5) 10 →(+7) 17 →(+9) 26.
(Equivalently the terms are n²+1: 1²+1=2, 2²+1=5, 3²+1=10, 4²+1=17, 5²+1=26.)

cards.front: Expand a perfect square (Q2.1.2): (2x + 1)². What is the pattern?
cards.back:
(2x + 1)² = (2x + 1)(2x + 1) = 4x² + 2x + 2x + 1 = 4x² + 4x + 1.
Pattern (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²: square the first (4x²), twice the product (2·2x·1 = 4x), square the last (1). The two middle terms are always equal.
cards.source: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016
cards.sourceFile: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016.yml

cards.back:
FOIL = First, Outer, Inner, Last:
F: 2x·3x = 6x²;  O: 2x·2 = 4x;  I: −1·3x = −3x;  L: −1·2 = −2.
(2x − 1)(3x + 2) = 6x² + 4x − 3x − 2 = 6x² + x − 2.
Combine the like middle terms 4x − 3x = x.

cards.back:
(2x−5)(x−3) = 2x²−6x−5x+15 = 2x²−11x+15.
(x+2)⁰ = 1 (anything to power 0 is 1).
(x−2)² = x²−4x+4, and we subtract it: −(x²−4x+4) = −x²+4x−4.
Combine: 2x²−11x+15 + 1 − x²+4x−4 = x² − 7x + 12.
KEY: keep the bracket on −(x−2)² so all signs flip correctly.

Dividing by ½ is multiplying by 2 (put the whole number over 1, flip the fraction):
10x³ ÷ ½x² = 10x³ ÷ (x²/2) = (10x³/1) × (2/x²) = 20x^(3−2) = 20x.
Tip: ÷ a fraction = × its reciprocal; subtract exponents for the same base.

Denominator: 3x × 4y = 12xy.

cards.front: Simplify the algebraic fraction (Q2.2.3): (6x² − 24)/(3x² + 6x). Why must you factorise first?
cards.back:
You can only cancel FACTORS, not terms — so factorise top and bottom first:
Top: 6x² − 24 = 6(x² − 4) = 6(x + 2)(x − 2)  [difference of squares].
Bottom: 3x² + 6x = 3x(x + 2).
= [6(x+2)(x−2)] / [3x(x+2)] = cancel 3 and (x+2): = 2(x − 2)/x.
Never cancel across a + or − sign.
cards.source: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016
cards.sourceFile: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016.yml

cards.back:
Simplify each fraction first.
First: 8x²y / 12xy² = (8/12)x^(2−1)y^(1−2) = (2/3)x/y = 2x/(3y).
Second: 6x² / 18xy = (6/18)x^(2−1)/y = (1/3)x/y = x/(3y).
Same denominator (3y), so add numerators: 2x/(3y) + x/(3y) = 3x/(3y) = x/y.
Always check at the end whether the result simplifies (3x/3y → x/y).
cards.source: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016

cards.front: Word problem (Q2.3): An isosceles triangle has two equal sides each = 2x² + 2x and perimeter = 7x² + 10x. Find the third side in terms of x.
cards.back:
Perimeter P = sum of all 3 sides.
Third side = P − (sum of the two equal sides)
= (7x² + 10x) − (2x² + 2x + 2x² + 2x)
= 7x² + 10x − (4x² + 4x)
= 7x² + 10x − 4x² − 4x
= 3x² + 6x.
Keep the bracket so both subtracted terms change sign.
cards.source: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016
cards.sourceFile: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016.yml

cards.back:
Find the highest common factor of the coefficients and variables: HCF of 2x² and 14x is 2x.
2x² + 14x = 2x(x + 7).
Check by expanding: 2x·x + 2x·7 = 2x² + 14x. ✓

cards.front: Factorise a difference of squares twice (Q3.2): x⁴ − 16.
cards.back:
Difference of squares a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b):
x⁴ − 16 = (x²)² − 4² = (x² + 4)(x² − 4).
The second factor is ITSELF a difference of squares: x² − 4 = (x + 2)(x − 2).
Final: x⁴ − 16 = (x² + 4)(x + 2)(x − 2).
(x² + 4 is a SUM of squares and cannot be factorised further.)
cards.source: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016
cards.sourceFile: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016.yml

4x² − 36 = 4(x² − 9) = 4(x + 3)(x − 3).

Notice (3y − 2x) = −(2x − 3y). Rewrite to expose the common bracket:
(2x − 3y)x² + (3y − 2x) = (2x − 3y)x² − (2x − 3y) = (2x − 3y)(x² − 1).
Then x² − 1 is a difference of squares: = (2x − 3y)(x + 1)(x − 1).

cards.front: Solve with brackets on both sides (Q4.1.2): 3(x + 2) = 2 − 1(x + 4).
cards.back:
Expand both sides: 3x + 6 = 2 − x − 4 → 3x + 6 = −x − 2.
Gather x's left, numbers right: 3x + x = −2 − 6 → 4x = −8 → x = −2.
Check: LHS 3(0) = 0; RHS 2 − 1(2) = 0. ✓ Remember −1(x + 4) = −x − 4.
cards.source: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016
cards.sourceFile: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016.yml

cards.back:
RHS = 2x² + x² + 12 = 3x² + 12. Equation: 3(x + 2) = 3x² + 12 → 3x + 6 = 3x² + 12.
Divide both sides by 3: x + 2 = x² + 4 → 0 = x² − x + 2.
Discriminant: (−1)² − 4(1)(2) = 1 − 8 = −7 < 0, so there is NO real solution. (At Gr 9 level: state no real solution.)

Simplify and clear denominators (LCD = 12). Note 2x/4 = x/2 and −4/6 = −2/3.
Multiply every term by 12: 12(x/2) + 12(1/3) = 12(−2/3) → 6x + 4 = −8.
6x = −12 → x = −2.
Check: (2·−2)/4 + 1/3 = −1 + 1/3 = −2/3 = −4/6. ✓

Simplify LHS by dividing each term by x: (2x² + x)/x = 2x + 1.
So 2x + 1 = (4x² + 3)/(2x). Multiply both sides by 2x: 2x(2x + 1) = 4x² + 3 → 4x² + 2x = 4x² + 3.
Subtract 4x²: 2x = 3 → x = 3/2.
(x ≠ 0 is required since we divided by x.)

cards.front: Set up an equation from words (Q4.2.1): x + 9 orange and 2x − 3 yellow jellybeans are in a packet with a total of 2(x + 8) yellow-and-orange jellybeans. Write the equation.
cards.back:
Total = orange + yellow:
(x + 9) + (2x − 3) = 2(x + 8).
Simplify the left: 3x + 6 = 2(x + 8). (You translate 'a total of' into an = sign, sum the two given quantities on one side.)
cards.source: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016
cards.sourceFile: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016.yml

cards.front: Solve and answer (Q4.2.2): from 3x + 6 = 2(x + 8), how many orange jellybeans (x + 9) are in the packet?
cards.back:
3x + 6 = 2x + 16 → 3x − 2x = 16 − 6 → x = 10.
Favourite colour is orange: orange jellybeans = x + 9 = 10 + 9 = 19.
Always substitute x back into the quantity the question actually asks for.
cards.source: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016
cards.sourceFile: Exam Paper D1 Algebra - Gr9 Maths 2-in-1_pages-015-016.yml

cards.front: Ratio word problem (Q4.3.1): games won : games lost = 5 : 1, and they only lost x + 4 games. How many games did the girls win, in terms of x?
cards.back:
Won : lost = 5 : 1, so won = 5 × lost.
Lost = x + 4, therefore won = 5(x + 4) = 5x + 20 games.
Multiply the lost quantity by the won-side of the ratio.
